headline: Shift Data Center Energy Costs to Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of grid upgrades and capacity procurement to large energy users, primarily data centers, rather than residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Senator Mark Warner, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling.
opponents: Large energy users (data centers, heavy industry), utility companies.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill seeks to reduce residential energy bills by requiring data centers to cover more of their electricity costs, including substations and capacity costs. If passed, residential customers could save over $5.50 monthly, while data center costs would increase significantly.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to report monthly water consumption by data centers to enhance transparency and aid water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, transparency advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, making the information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about data centers' significant water consumption and provide transparency for communities.

headline: Establish Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for sound profiles and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Del. Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Data Center Bills Led 2026 Virginia General Assembly
news_summary: The 2026 Virginia legislative session focused heavily on data center regulation, with HB 153 introducing new siting requirements for large data centers. This bill mandates impact assessments on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval, laying the groundwork for future regulations on data center placement and community impact.
